1. generation (n)
/ˌdʒenəˈreɪʃn/
thế hệ (ông bà, cha mẹ, con cái)
Collocation: younger generation, generation gap
"Clear communication helps bridge the generation gap between parents and teenagers."
2. nuclear (adj)
/ˈnjuːkliə(r)/
hạt nhân (gia đình 2 thế hệ: bố mẹ và con)
Collocation: nuclear family, modern nuclear household
"In large cities, most young couples prefer living in a small nuclear family."
3. extended (adj)
/ɪkˈstendɪd/
mở rộng, đại gia đình (nhiều thế hệ cùng chung sống)
Collocation: extended family, traditional extended household
"Growing up in an extended family taught me to respect my grandparents."
4. upbringing (n)
/ˈʌpbrɪŋɪŋ/
sự nuôi dạy, giáo dục từ thuở nhỏ trong gia đình
Collocation: strict upbringing, warm family upbringing
"A supportive upbringing gives children strong confidence in their adult lives."
5. sibling (n)
/ˈsɪblɪŋ/
anh chị em ruột trong gia đình
Collocation: older sibling, sibling rivalry
"Children who grow up with siblings learn how to share toys and resolve arguments."
6. adolescence (n)
/ˌædəˈlesns/
thời thanh thiếu niên, tuổi dậy thì
Collocation: during adolescence, early adolescence
"During adolescence, young people often seek greater independence from their parents."
7. nurture (v)
/ˈnɜːtʃə(r)/
nuôi dưỡng, chăm sóc và bồi đắp tình cảm/tài năng
Collocation: nurture young children, nurture talent
"Both parents should share the duty to nurture and guide their children."
8. conflict (n)
/ˈkɒnflɪkt/
sự xung đột, mâu thuẫn, bất đồng quan điểm
Collocation: family conflict, resolve a conflict
"Different views on career choices can sometimes cause conflict between generations."
9. bond (n)
/bɒnd/
sợi dây gắn kết, mối liên kết tình cảm bền chặt
Collocation: strong family bond, emotional bond
"Eating dinner together every evening strengthens the emotional bond within a family."
10. household (n)
/ˈhaʊshəʊld/
hộ gia đình, công việc nội trợ trong nhà
Collocation: household chores, low-income household
"In modern families, husbands and wives divide household chores equally."
11. supportive (adj)
/səˈpɔːtɪv/
luôn ủng hộ, nâng đỡ và cảm thông
Collocation: supportive parents, mutually supportive
"My parents were extremely supportive when I decided to study architecture."
12. independent (adj)
/ˌɪndɪˈpendənt/
tự lập, độc lập (về tài chính hoặc lối sống)
Collocation: financially independent, become independent
"University life teaches young adults to become more independent and self-reliant."
13. harmony (n)
/ˈhɑːməni/
sự hòa thuận, êm ấm, hài hòa
Collocation: live in harmony, domestic harmony
"Mutual respect allows three generations to live together in peace and harmony."
14. influential (adj)
/ˌɪnfluˈenʃl/
có sức ảnh hưởng lớn
Collocation: highly influential, influential role model
"Parents are the most influential role models during a child's early years."
15. responsibility (n)
/rɪˌspɒnsəˈbɪləti/
trách nhiệm, bổn phận
Collocation: take responsibility for, parental responsibility
"Caring for elderly grandparents is considered an important family responsibility."

⚙️ 2. Bài Giảng Ngữ Pháp 2 Tầng (Grammar Masterclass)

🟢 Tầng 1: Căn Bản (Cấp So Sánh Hơn, So Sánh Nhất & So Sánh Bằng)

• So sánh hơn (Comparative): Dùng khi đối chiếu 2 đối tượng (ví dụ: gia đình hạt nhân vs đại gia đình).
  - Tính từ ngắn (1 âm tiết): Adj-er + than (smaller than, closer than).
  - Tính từ dài (≥ 2 âm tiết): more / less + Adj + than (more independent than, more supportive than).
  Ví dụ: Young people today become financially more independent than previous generations.

• So sánh nhất (Superlative): the + Adj-est hoặc the most + Adj.
  Ví dụ: Parents play the most influential role in a child's early upbringing.

• So sánh bằng (Equal Comparison): as + Adj/Adv + as (Phủ định: not as/so + Adj + as).
  Ví dụ: Modern nuclear families are not as large as traditional extended households.

🔵 Tầng 2: Nâng Cao (Trạng Từ Nhấn Mạnh Cấp So Sánh & Cấu Trúc Whereas / While)

• Nhấn mạnh mức độ chênh lệch (Modifiers in Comparisons): Đặt much / far / significantly / considerably trước tính từ so sánh hơn để nâng điểm ngữ pháp lên Band 6.0+.
  Ví dụ: Living in a nuclear family is much more flexible than living in a large extended household.

• Liên từ đối chiếu hai chiều While / Whereas (Trong khi đó):
  Ví dụ: While extended families offer strong childcare support, nuclear households provide greater personal privacy.

🎯 20 Câu Test Từ Vựng (Vocabulary Mastery Test)

1. A ________ family consists of only parents and their children living under one roof.
2. In rural areas, many people still live in an ________ family with grandparents, aunts, and uncles.
3. Open conversations at the dinner table help reduce the ________ gap between parents and teenagers.
4. Sharing daily ________ chores such as cooking and cleaning helps keep a marriage happy.
5. Having an older ________ taught me how to share books and cooperate with others from an early age.
6. A warm and disciplined ________ prepares children to face challenges in adulthood.
7. During ________, teenagers experience rapid physical and emotional changes.
8. Spending quality time together on weekends builds a strong emotional ________ between parents and children.
9. When three generations live together, differences in lifestyle can occasionally cause family ________.
10. Good teachers and parents work together to ________ a child's natural curiosity and kindness.
11. My family has always been very ________ of my dream to study medicine abroad.
12. Many university students take part-time jobs so they can become financially ________.
13. Mutual patience and kindness allow neighbours and family members to live in ________.
14. Grandparents often play a highly ________ role in passing down cultural traditions to grandchildren.
15. Looking after sick relatives is seen as a moral ________ in many Asian cultures.
16. [Ôn tập Unit 1] Sharing meals is an important part of our family's daily ________.
17. [Ôn tập Unit 2] Strong self-________ helps students finish homework without parental reminders.
18. [Ôn tập Unit 3] Parents should teach children to protect the natural ________ and recycle waste.
19. [Ôn tập Unit 4] Cooking fresh meals at home provides better ________ than eating fast food.
20. [Ôn tập Unit 5] Video calls allow relatives living abroad to ________ with their family every day.
Điểm: 0/20

⚙️ 10 Câu Test Ngữ Pháp Ứng Dụng (Grammar Mastery Test)

1. Modern nuclear households are usually much ________ than traditional extended families.
2. Parents are often the ________ role models during a child's early upbringing.
3. Living alone in a big city is not as ________ as living with supportive family members.
4. Young adults today tend to become financially ________ than their parents were at the same age.
5. ________ extended families provide daily childcare support, nuclear families offer greater personal privacy.
6. Resolving family conflicts calmly is far ________ than shouting in anger.
7. Among all my relatives, my grandmother is the ________ person I have ever known.
8. Sharing household chores equally makes family life significantly ________ and more harmonious.
9. For working parents, professional childcare centres are often ________ expensive than help from grandparents.
10. Siblings who grow up sharing responsibilities often develop a ________ bond than children who never share.
Điểm: 0/10

👨 Participant: My pleasure! I find changes in family structure across generations really fascinating.
👩 Researcher: First, may I record your surname? Is it spelled Miller?
👨 Participant: Actually, it is Bennett. That is spelled B - E - N - N - E - T - T. 💡 Bẫy đính chính & đánh vần câu 1: BENNETT

👩 Researcher: And how many siblings did you have during your childhood upbringing?
👨 Participant: I have two older brothers and one younger sister, so I had three siblings in total. 💡 Đáp án câu 3: 3 / three
👩 Researcher: In your current home, what is the most effective way to maintain family harmony?
👨 Participant: We share all household chores equally and eat dinner together without phones every evening. 💡 Đáp án câu 4: dinner / eating dinner
👩 Researcher: What do you think causes the most common conflict between parents and teenagers during adolescence?

👩 Researcher: Finally, which family member had the most influential impact on your education?

📰 IELTS Academic Reading: Passage & Questions

[Paragraph A - The Shift in Household Structure]
Over the past century, family structures around the world have changed dramatically. In the past, most people grew up in a traditional extended family, where three generations lived under one roof. Grandparents played a highly influential role in a child's upbringing, while cousins and siblings shared daily work. Today, rapid urbanization has made the smaller nuclear family much more common, as young couples move to cities to become financially independent.

[Paragraph B - Benefits and Challenges of Modern Families]
Both family models have distinct advantages. Living in a nuclear household gives parents greater privacy and freedom to decide how to nurture their children. However, without grandparents nearby, working parents often carry a heavier childcare responsibility. Furthermore, during adolescence, teenagers who spend too much time alone online may experience a weaker emotional bond with their relatives and face occasional family conflict.

[Paragraph C - Building Domestic Harmony]
Sociologists emphasize that whether a family is large or small, mutual respect is the key to domestic harmony. When husbands and wives are supportive of each other and divide household chores fairly, children grow up in a warm environment. Regular family meals and weekend outings remain the best ways to keep every generation closely connected.
Điểm: 0/6
